rows.quote: SULTAN (from the German SUpraLeiter Test ANlage) is the reference magnet facility for testing forced-flow, high-current superconductors up to fields of 10.8 T.
rows.value_as_printed: What we Test: Forced-flow and cable-in-conduit conductor samples, including joints
rows.document_title: EPFL Swiss Plasma Center, SULTAN Test Facility
rows.location: Intro paragraph and 'What we Test' list (cached research/v5/cache/ce76339ad6b5a8a0.txt)
rows.reasoning: The facility owner's page positively defines SULTAN as a split-solenoid magnet facility for testing forced-flow / cable-in-conduit superconductor samples and joints (DC performance, AC loss, quench energy, cyclic loading). Its full 'What we Test' list and the Testing Services page (conductor samples, small coils, anti-cryostat special samples) contain no cryopump test stand or controlled test-gas admission; it is a different kind of instrument from the ITER cryopump test facility the experiment requires.

Searched the EPFL SULTAN page and Testing Services page (cached ce76339ad6b5a8a0, abe94908d0728b12), the ITER 'Evaluating the ITER magnets at SULTAN' article, the SOFT 2010 Bruzzone abstract (P2-154), Infoscience/graphsearch SULTAN records, WebSearch for SULTAN test well/insulation vacuum/anti-cryostat, and Lune paper search. Sources describe a test well, cryostat and an anti-cryostat filled with He gas, but none states verbatim that the sample space is evacuated; Tavily was over quota. No sourced value or positive absence, so left unknown.
